tagline: Four lanes along the marsh edge of the Great Salt Lake.
intro: Legacy Parkway runs south from Farmington toward Salt Lake City with I-15 and the rail lines on one side and the wetlands of the Great Salt Lake on the other. It bends to follow the edge of the marsh, past the Farmington Bay Waterfowl Management Area, with protected wetland west of the pavement and in the median, and a trail beside it the whole way.

Millions of migrating birds stop at the lake each spring and fall, treating it, in Visit Utah's phrase, as a huge cafeteria. The road was a long argument. It went to court several times, and the settlement with the Sierra Club held it to four lanes and kept semi-trucks off until 2020.

moments.title: Farmington
moments.text: The parkway ends west of Lagoon, which began in 1886 as Lake Park on the lakeshore, until the lake drew back so far that the resort closed and its buildings were moved about three miles east.

moments.title: Centerville
moments.text: First called Deuel Settlement and then Cherry Creek, the town took its present name after an 1850 survey found it exactly halfway between Farmington and Bountiful.

moments.title: Legacy Nature Preserve
moments.text: Near the south end the parkway itself forms the eastern border of the preserve, protected land that was enlarged when the road was rerouted after the court fights.
